rules.title: Notice to Tenant of Residential Tenant Protections
rules.requirement: A landlord of covered residential rental property must give tenants a written notice, in no less than 12-point font, stating that local law requires a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy, together with a copy of the Tenant Protection Guide. For tenancies existing before June 24, 2023 the notice was due within 90 days of June 24, 2023; for tenancies commencing or renewed on or after June 24, 2023 it must be included in the lease or given as a signed written notice at lease signing.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property subject to Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 of the San Diego Municipal Code.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to comply with any provision of this Division shall render void any notice of termination required by this Division.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall provide written notice in no less than 12-point font to the tenant, and in a manner that complies with California Civil Code section 1632, as may be amended, that states as follows:

rules.title: Requirements Upon Termination of Tenancy for At-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: Before issuing a notice to terminate for an at-fault just cause that is a curable lease violation, the landlord must first give written notice describing the violation and an opportunity to cure; if not cured, the landlord may terminate by serving a three-day notice to quit. The landlord must also notify the Commission of the at-fault termination no later than three business days after notifying the tenant.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property subject to this Division who issue a termination notice for at-fault just cause.
rules.exemptions: The Commission notice requirement in section 98.0706(a)(2) does not apply until 30 days after the Commission establishes a submission portal and provides public notice of its creation.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall render void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706, in addition to other remedies.
rules.quoted_span: Before a landlord issues a notice to terminate a tenancy for at-fault just cause that is a curable lease violation, the landlord shall first give written notice of the violation including a description of the violation and an opportunity to cure the violation under California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161(3), as may be amended. If the violation is not cured within the time period in the notice, the landlord may terminate the tenancy without another opportunity to cure by serving a three-day notice to quit.

rules.title: Notice Requirements Upon Termination of Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the landlord must give the tenant written notice at least 30 or 60 days before the termination date as required by California Civil Code section 1946.1, in no less than 12-point font, describing the basis for termination and stating the tenant's right to relocation assistance and to an offer to renew if the unit is re-offered for rent within five years. The landlord must also notify the Commission no later than three business days after notifying the tenant.
rules.key_value: at least 30 or 60 days prior to the proposed date of termination
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property subject to this Division who issue a termination notice for no-fault just cause.
rules.exemptions: The Commission notice requirement in section 98.0706(b)(2) does not apply until 30 days after the Commission establishes a submission portal and provides public notice of its creation.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall render void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706, in addition to other remedies.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall give written notice to the tenant at least 30 or 60 days prior to the proposed date of termination as required by California Civil Code section 1946.1, as may be amended, in no less than 12-point font.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for Termination of Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the landlord must, regardless of the tenant's income or length of tenancy, provide relocation assistance either as a direct payment within 15 days of the notice or as a rent waiver, equal to two months of actual rent, or three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled. Relocation assistance is in addition to return of any deposit and is credited against other relocation assistance required by federal, state or other local law.
rules.key_value: Two months of actual rent; three months of actual rent if the tenant is a senior or disabled
rules.coverage_text: Tenants of residential rental property subject to this Division whose tenancy is terminated for no-fault just cause, regardless of income or length of tenancy.
rules.penalty: Any landlord who fails to provide relocation assistance as required by section 98.0706(c) shall be liable to the tenant in a civil action for not less than three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic damages.
rules.quoted_span: Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
rules.interaction_text: Any relocation assistance required by this Division shall be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any federal, state, or other local law.

rules.title: Right to Offer to Renew After No-Fault Just Cause Termination
rules.requirement: If the unit is offered for rent within five years of an eviction under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), the landlord must first offer it in writing to the displaced tenant, provided the tenant asked in writing within 30 days of the termination notice and gave a mailing or email address. The tenant has 30 days from receipt of the offer to accept, and the landlord may screen using industry accepted methods.
rules.key_value: within five years of the date the tenant was evicted
rules.coverage_text: Tenants displaced by a no-fault just cause termination under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4) from residential rental property subject to this Division.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall render void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706, in addition to other remedies.

rules.title: Buyout Agreements
rules.requirement: Before making a buyout offer the landlord must give each tenant a written disclosure of their rights, and any buyout agreement must be in writing with specified statements, and must be for an amount greater than the relocation assistance available under section 98.0706(c). A buyout agreement for less than the relocation assistance owed, or that does not strictly comply with the requirements, is void, and the provisions may not be waived.
rules.key_value: Buyout amount must be greater than the relocation assistance available under section 98.0706(c)
rules.coverage_text: Landlords making buyout offers to tenants in residential rental property subject to this Division.
rules.penalty: A buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed to the tenant violates this Division and is void; a buyout agreement that does not strictly comply with section 98.0707(c)(1)-(4) shall be void.
rules.quoted_span: Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c). A buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed to the tenant violates this Division and is void.
